analysis.title: The Bounce Fixed Nothing
key_insights: The equity squeeze is losing momentum: tech is running into major resistance and the broader market remains in its range, while the dollar is breaking out, yields are surging and liquidity is deteriorating.

SPX remains inside the trading range in place since May. The latest squeeze reached almost the 100-day MA, but the index is still in the middle of the range, so The Market Ear sees little risk/reward edge and stays in watch mode.

NDX reversed at the 200-day MA and is struggling to re-enter the range. It printed its biggest down candle since the bounce began. First short-term support is the 27,500 area (futures), then the 26,500 zone.

BofA's Hartnett highlights a global tightening cycle that is far from over, with more than 70 rate hikes expected between June 2026 and May 2027. The April FOMC is the earliest potential turning point.
A surging dollar and gold below $4,000 signal retreating global liquidity. Sticky CPI leaves little room for lower Treasury yields to rescue risk assets, even with oil down 15%.

Cyclicals are weak per Hartnett: lumber -21%, metals -11% and blue-collar semis -26%. Consensus still expects 5-6% nominal GDP growth and more than 15% EPS growth in 2027, so the next revision looks more likely to be down than up.

The dollar is breaking out of a multi-year trading range, and two-year Treasury yields posted their biggest two-day advance in more than two years after the hotter CPI print. Tech and semis are struggling to reclaim key technical levels.

SocGen's Albert Edwards says excess liquidity has deteriorated sharply and has historically been a decent leading indicator for equities. The relationship is imperfect, and the liquidity backdrop is worsening as the AI trade wobbles.

Edwards notes that year-on-year core inflation still looks benign but shorter-term measures are moving higher. Corporate output-price inflation has stayed above 4%. Another inflation surprise could leave the Fed facing sticky prices and weak equities together.
BTC did not participate in the equity squeeze and continued to slide, suggesting its sensitivity to risk appetite is returning.
Hartnett says investors are only emotionally bearish: equity inflows were the biggest weekly inflow since June.
Volatility has retreated from Thursday's panic extremes but remains elevated, particularly in tech. The options market is still pricing considerable uncertainty.

Nomura's McElligott argues the volatility regime has shifted: the VIX floor may have moved from 15-16 to around 18, and the VVIX floor from the 80-90s toward the mid-90s. This implies wider daily ranges and more violent two-way moves, with rallies potentially as aggressive as sell-offs.

tension_points.bull_case: The bounce relieved oversold conditions, equity inflows were the biggest weekly inflow since June, and a higher vol regime could make rallies as aggressive as sell-offs.
tension_points.bear_case: The dollar is breaking out, 2-year yields have surged, liquidity is deteriorating, NDX was rejected at the 200-day MA, BTC did not join the bounce and consensus 2027 growth looks too high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained move above the 200-day MA on NDX would challenge the bear read. The source frames its own downside levels at 27,500 and then 26,500 for NDX futures.
